newsitem.title: MEXICO: G.E. Capital buys control of Mexican bank.
newsitem.headline: G.E. Capital buys control of Mexican bank.

text.p: G.E. Capital on Monday said it had bought control for 210 million pesos of Mexico's Banco Alianza, a small bank owned by Tamulipas businessman Sergio Arguelles Gutierrez.
It said the payment was made to Alianza shareholders, both Mexican and foreign.
Alianza was set up on Dec. 17, 1994, just three days before the peso devaluation, with start-up capital of 130 million pesos. Unlike most larger banks in the system, it has no past-due loans.
A statement said its shareholders made a profit on their original investment.
They decided to sell the bank because banking in Mexico has become a business for large financial groups, and because capital requirements are increasingly intense, Arguelles said.
The deal was completed on Monday, and GE Capital plans to begin operations with the bank immediately.
